newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Transtech Electronics aims for Singapore listing.
newsitem.headline: Transtech Electronics aims for Singapore listing.

text.p: Manufacturer Transtech Electronics Pte Ltd intends to apply for a listing on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) in the third quarter this year, managing director Alan Tan said on Thursday.
"We've appointed a merchant bank and auditor and hope that by end-April we can submit our application," Tan told reporters at the opening of the company's business headquarters in Singapore.

He said the Singapore-based company hoped to raise about Singapore $18 million from an initial public offer. It aimed to float 25 percent of the company's share capital for a mainboard listing around August.
Transtech is a contract manufacturer for Japanese firms like AIWA and supplies a wide range of products such as computer peripherals, telecommunication and high-end audio equipment.
The proceeds would go to product development, prototyping, instrumentation and engineer expenses, Tan said.
Tan said the company had appointed Development Bank of Singapore to handle its listing.
Transtech recorded a group turnover of S$429 million in 1996, and Tan said sales were expected to improve over the next two years along with the recovery in the global electronics industry.
"This year we should be able to perform better than last year," Tan said, noting that excess electronic supplies in the market had been mostly absorbed after a spell of overproduction.
He said manufacturers had pushed output to keep their profits from dwindling during the economic slowdown, and this situation looked to be reversing.
Manufacturing will now be focused on the company's key new products, namely in-jet printer heads and flat panel television displays, and also cordless phones and CD-ROM's, he said.
Transtech has six factories in Malaysia. It owns a 40 percent stake in Malaysian-listed Tru-Tech Holdings.
Tan said the company's net tangible assets in Malaysia were around RM80 million (S$32.3 million), and facilities there would continue to handle the bulk of the company's manufacturing.
Its headquarters in Singapore would concentrate on research and development and production of value-added products, Tan said.
Transtech's headquarters are part of the company's $$40 million investment plan to establish a one-stop business hub in Singapore.
